findings.title: L1 larder takes the queen's R2 hand-over protein into a rotting pile; viability 4 -> 1 of 15 on the same hand-overs
findings.detail: Before L1, a nest with no food chamber held P only in the social stomachs, so most of the queen's provision stayed in her body and went into the pool as larvae ate. With the larder (>= 4 loads) the pool takes it all at once, on the brood chamber floor, where it spoils; the queen refills what rots. Probe on the cpv #1 hand-over: 1.98 P spoiled before the first larva hatched (0 without L1); larvae got 7.9 P vs 9.85 by h72; about 4 spoiled-food items among the eggs. 15-pair A/B with the round's 12 production files reverted (same tree otherwise, same hand-overs): viable 1 vs 4, workers at winter 128 vs 154 (held 2 vs 7), eclosions 35 vs 56, larvae starved 48 vs 7, median bad-stage 3.55 vs 0.10 gd, larva:hygiene 28 vs 4. Reverting L1 alone (4 pairs): eclosions 14 -> 24, starved 7 -> 0. New test src/sim/colony/larderProvision.verify.test.ts is RED on the tree (1.39 P spoiled, 2 items in 1.5 gd) and green without L1.

findings.title: WL1 lapse cap: the workers the cap keeps eat nothing over the winter
findings.where: src/sim/colony/overwinter/begin.ts beginOverwinter (takes model c1/p1, then caps losses)
findings.detail: The model's spring stores are computed with the drawn losses; the cap then keeps those workers alive without charging their food. In src/sim/colony/overwinter/lossCapStores.verify.test.ts (RED): seed 1 ends with 17 vs 9 workers and the same C, 16.554; seed 5 with 17 vs 6. So spring stores are overstated, which is free food in effect, and R27's stores check gets the wrong number.

findings.title: M1 2D midden test also covers waste inside the nest under the surface midden
findings.detail: haulMidden.verify.test.ts (RED): waste on a cavity floor 10 BU under the midden point reads as at the midden (haul priority 0). Latent: on the 15 R20 hand-overs there is no midden at hand-over, and the founding chamber is 8 BU from the entrance.

findings.title: H4 round test did not exercise the trigger (coverage gap, now closed)
findings.detail: It stays green with broodAmongWaste unwired. New hygieneWiring.verify.test.ts goes through allocateColony on a real nest: green on the tree, red with the trigger unwired. The trigger works.
